_comment: Per-score options of `python3 -m pianovision build` (pianovision/buildopts.py). Keys of 'scores' are score
paths relative to the scores folder; keys starting with '_' are comments. Only what build makes of a score
title, composer   the song's title and composer (PianoVision's name/artist and the output name)
piano_staves      the staves (1-based) that are the piano part, right hand first; the others are orchestra
hands             'staves' (default) or 'split': the piano part's notes to the hands by pitch and reach
simplified_from   a piano arrangement (score path) that becomes the simplified part, measure-aligned
measure_map       'auto', or {pin: [[arr, orch], ...], fill: [orch, ...], drop: [arr, ...]} with measures
as the scores number them ('12', '12-30', '395:2' = the second pass): see the report in

Gershwin/Rhapsody_in_blue__George_Gershw.title: Rhapsody in Blue (Piano and Orchestra)
Gershwin/Rhapsody_in_blue__George_Gershw._title: its own title would collide with the piano solo (gers_Rhapsody_in_Blue.json); its metadata's workTitle says 'Second Rhapsody' (wrong)
Gershwin/Rhapsody_in_blue__George_Gershw._simplified_from: the piano solo arrangement, measure-aligned, is the default (simplified) part; the measures it leaves out play the orchestral score's Solo Piano part

Rachmaninoff/pagvar18.mscz.title: Rhapsody on a Theme of Paganini - Var. XVIII (Piano and Orchestra)
Rachmaninoff/pagvar18.mscz._title: a MIDI import without title or composer; named like the piano solo version (rach_Rhapsody_on_a_Theme_of_Paganini__Var_XVIII.json), which stays a song of its own
Rachmaninoff/pagvar18.mscz._piano: 'Piano, Roland Piano' (staves 11-12) is the solo piano: alone in m. 1-12, about a quarter of its onsets coincide with the orchestra's. The import wrote both hands on staff 11 (clef changes every measure; staff 12 has the overflow), so the hands are split by pitch and reach. 'Piano' (staff 1) holds one stray E-flat 5 in m. 33 doubling the violins: orchestra by its program
